## H7 — Legal Next Action
The legal next action is to execute slice `S1` within its allowed paths, `guide.md` and `commands.txt`, stopping immediately on scope drift. The executor must not declare the goal complete.

## H8 — Non-Goals / Forbidden Scope
No work beyond the stated documentation change is authorized. The following paths are forbidden:

- `.tad/scripts/`
- `.claude/`
- `.tad/hooks/`

Starting other slices, redoing verified work, inspecting hidden acceptance, or changing unrelated content is forbidden.

## S1 — Why the Next Action Is Legal
Appending the specified section and table to `guide.md`, while consulting `commands.txt`, exactly matches the current `S1` contract, maps directly to `SC-1`, and stays within the two allowed paths.

## S2 — Why Verified Work Must Not Be Redone
Governance explicitly prohibits redoing verified work because verified state may advance only through a bound receipt from a Conductor distinct from the executor. There is currently no verified work to repeat.

## S3 — Why Blind Retry / Self-Completion Is Unavailable
No failed execution or retry authorization is recorded; the journal shows only initialization and preparation of the first slice. A blind retry therefore has no ledger basis. Self-completion is unavailable because executor prose, file state, checkpoints, and self-authored receipts cannot advance verification or establish completion.

## S4 — Rejected
Rejected actions include treating the observed target state or any uncommitted changes as progress, declaring completion, inventing verification, blindly retrying, starting another slice, modifying existing introductory content, touching paths outside the slice contract or forbidden paths, spawning agents, using prohibited Phase-2 shell execution, and searching for hidden acceptance.
